reason: S1 removes the initializer entry points called by H0 and replaces them with a protocol that requires caller-zeroed state plus a sizeof argument. Consequently, H0 cannot invoke the S1 GIF or zlib decoder initialization APIs as written, and simply renaming the calls would leave the stack-allocated dec objects uninitialized.
evidence: gif_fuzzer.c calls wuffs_gif__decoder__initialize(&dec, WUFFS_VERSION, 0), but S1 replaces that symbol with wuffs_gif__decoder__check_wuffs_version(..., size_t sizeof_star_self).
zlib_fuzzer.c calls wuffs_zlib__decoder__initialize(&dec, WUFFS_VERSION, 0), but S1 replaces that symbol with wuffs_zlib__decoder__check_wuffs_version(..., size_t sizeof_star_self).

The removed initialize implementations conditionally called memset(self, 0, sizeof(*self)); the replacement check_wuffs_version implementations no longer clear self and only set private_impl.magic after validating WUFFS_VERSION and sizeof(*self).
Both harnesses declare decoder objects as uninitialized stack variables: wuffs_gif__decoder dec and wuffs_zlib__decoder dec.
S0 provided exactly the initialize symbols and three-argument protocol used by H0, while S1 removes them, so the gap is introduced by this commit rather than historical.
recommended_action: Update both fuzz functions to zero-initialize dec, then call the corresponding wuffs_gif__decoder__check_wuffs_version or wuffs_zlib__decoder__check_wuffs_version with WUFFS_VERSION and sizeof(dec) before invoking decoder operations.
